title: Mosiah Grants Permission to Inquire
summary: After three years of continual peace, Mosiah wants to know about the people who went to Lehi-Nephi. His people have heard nothing from them since they left Zarahemla and weary him with their teasings. Mosiah grants permission for sixteen strong men to go and inquire about their brethren.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah had had continual peace for three years.
He wanted to know about the people who went to dwell in the land or city of Lehi-Nephi.
His people had heard nothing from them since they left Zarahemla and wearied him with their teasings.
Mosiah granted that sixteen of their strong men might go to Lehi-Nephi to inquire about their brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah may be shown with unnamed members of his people as they weary him with their teasings.
unspecified_visual_details: The present setting, appearances, clothing, and architecture are not specified.

narration.text: his people had heard nothing from them from the time they left the land of Zarahemla; therefore, they wearied him with their teasings.

Do not depict the people in Lehi-Nephi as present with Mosiah.

title: Before King Limhi

Limhi says he preserved them so he could question them, and permits them to speak.

title: Treaty and Tribute Recounted
summary: The account recounts Zeniff’s deception, a treaty with king Laman, and possessions of part of the land yielded into Zeniff’s hands. It reports current tribute exacted by the king of the Lamanites: half the people’s corn, barley, grain of every kind, increase of flocks and herds, and all they have or possess—or their lives.

explicit_facts.text: The account describes Zeniff as having been made king over this people, overzealous to inherit the land of his fathers, and deceived by king Laman’s cunning and craftiness.

The account states that king Laman entered into a treaty with king Zeniff and yielded into his hands possessions of part of the land: the city of Lehi-Nephi, the city of Shilom, and the land round about.
Verse 22 attributes the sole purpose of bringing the people into subjection or bondage to “he,” without naming that referent within the verse.

The account reports current tribute to the king of the Lamanites amounting to one half of the people’s corn, barley, and grain of every kind; one half of the increase of their flocks and herds; and one half of all they have or possess, exacted of them or their lives.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The direct address permits a restrained depiction of an unidentified speaker addressing unspecified listeners, but does not establish their identities or physical arrangement.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether to depict the address visually rather than use a neutral presentation.
The speaker’s identity and appearance, listeners’ appearance, setting, clothing, and staging are unspecified.

title: The Slain Prophet Recounted
summary: A prophet was slain after condemning wickedness and abominations and prophesying of Christ's coming. He taught that Christ was God and would take upon himself the image of man, flesh and blood. Those who killed him also did other things that brought God's wrath upon them; their bondage and afflictions are recounted.

explicit_facts.text: A prophet of the Lord, described as a chosen man of God, was slain after telling people of their wickedness and abominations and prophesying of coming events, including Christ's coming.

The prophet taught that Christ was God, the Father of all things; that man was created after God's image; and that God would come among humankind, taking flesh and blood and going forth upon the earth.
The people put the prophet to death because of this teaching and did many other things that brought God's wrath upon them. Their bondage and sore afflictions are stated.
